script:
You are a professional screenwriter.

Write a modern screenplay.

Constraints:
- No guns
- No gun violence
- No weapon combat
- No graphic violence
- No copyrighted characters
- Completely original story

Requirements:
- 10–15 scenes
- Proper screenplay format
- INT/EXT scene headers
- Dialogue in uppercase character format
- Realistic pacing

Genre: Family
Theme: identity

Begin screenplay.

FADE IN:

EXT. SMALL TOWN - DAY

A quaint little village nestled in the rolling hills, surrounded by lush green forests and sparkling streams. We follow a young boy, JAMES (12), as he rides his bike down the main street, passing by colorful houses and friendly neighbors.

INT. JAMES' HOUSE - LIVING ROOM - DAY

James sits on the couch with his mother, LUCY (40). They share a quiet moment, looking at family photos scattered across the coffee table.

LUCY: (wistfully)
Do you ever wonder where your father is, James?

JAMES: (hesitantly)
He left when I was just a baby. I don't really remember him.

INT. LIBRARY - STUDY ROOM - DAY

James spends hours in the library, pouring over old town records and historical documents, searching for any information about his father. He makes a startling discovery - his father was a renowned artist, who once painted a beautiful mural in the town square.

INT. TOWN SQUARE - DAY

James stands in front of the mural, admiring the intricate details and stunning colors. A local resident, MRS. JOHNSON (65), approaches him.

MRS. JOHNSON: (smiling)
You seem to take great interest in that mural, young man. I used to know your father. He was quite the talented artist.

JAMES: (excitedly)
Really? Do you have any photos or memories you could share with me?

INT. MRS. JOHNSON'S HOUSE - LIVING ROOM - DAY

Mrs. Johnson shows James a box filled with old photographs, letters, and sketches, each one revealing a piece of his father's life. James listens intently as Mrs. Johnson shares stories about his father's passion for art and his dream of traveling the world.

INT. JAMES' HOUSE - LIVING ROOM - NIGHT

James sits at the dinner table with his mother and younger sister, ELLA (8). He shares what he's learned about their father, inspiring Ella to draw a picture for their absentee father.

INT. ART CLASS - SCHOOL - DAY

James joins an art class at school, where he learns various techniques and creates his first painting. His teacher, MR. PARKER (55), recognizes James' talent and encourages him to continue exploring his passion for art.

INT. TOWN SQUARE - DAY

James stands in front of the mural, painting alongside local artists, inspired by his newfound connection to his father. The community gathers around to watch him work, and James feels a sense of belonging and pride in his identity.

INT. JAMES' HOUSE - LIVING ROOM - NIGHT

James proudly displays his painting next to the family photos. Lucy looks at her son with tears in her eyes, finally seeing her husband's legacy living on through James.

INT. MUSEUM - EXHIBIT HALL - NIGHT

Years later, James is an accomplished artist, and his work is featured in a museum exhibit. His mother, sister, and the entire community gather to celebrate his achievements, proud of the identity he has discovered through his father's art.

FADE OUT.

THE END.
